description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 29, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: pydantic/pydantic-ai is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: pydantic/pydantic-ai leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: pydantic/pydantic-ai — 24 commits today, 4.7 above its current daily pace, with 18 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 147 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
Kilo-Org/kilocode — No same-day commit after 266 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Pi has a model router; the useful result is the task it finishes
dailyInsight.insight: Pi's new virtual-model example uses Jev to choose a planning model, then changes models after the first successful file edit. It makes a routing policy inspectable without establishing that the policy saves money at the same task quality.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The example thresholds a two-category complexity answer at 0.5, preserves the planning choice in session state, and moves to its implementation model after an edit or write succeeds. Scripted tests exercise the handoff, not classifier accuracy.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A lower-priced next call can still produce a more expensive completed task if classification, cache misses or an unsuitable handoff add work.

actions.audience: Teams considering Pi's experimental Jev router
actions.label: Look for a matched completed-task comparison
actions.instruction: Before adopting the example as a cost policy, require a comparison against a fixed model on the same tasks and acceptance criteria, including classifier calls, failed tasks, cache misses and all later attempts. Keep the fixed-model configuration as the baseline.
actions.effort: One evaluation plan before a routing-policy trial

receipts.title: Virtual models and the Jev routing example
receipts.supports: Introduces the virtual-model routing mechanism and a concrete planning-to-implementation policy.

receipts.title: Jev router source and operating assumptions
receipts.supports: Shows the complexity threshold, first-successful-edit trigger, persisted phase and provider credentials required by the example.

confidence.basis: The merged example and scripted regression definitions agree on the routing mechanism; completed-task economics remain unmeasured in this inspection.

dailyInsight.limitation: We inspected source and test definitions, without running the router or mapping it to an installed release. A binary probability threshold does not prove a need for a full distribution or calibrated confidence.
dailyInsight.falsifier: A matched completed-task evaluation showing that classifier overhead and misrouting erase the proposed savings would overturn the economic rationale for this policy; a policy or release change would require a new source check.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A public fixed-model versus routed-task evaluation with explicit acceptance criteria, full accounting and failure outcomes.
